title: Hierarchical Knowledge Injection for Improving LLM-based Program Repair
datasets: BugsInPy: 314 single-function bug/patch pairs from 16 projects; six annotated bug types.
task: Automated program repair by progressively injecting bug-level, repository-level and project-level context; manual bug-type analysis and unresolved-bug complexity analysis.
input_setting: Buggy function with perfect function-level localization; first add bug/test/error/runtime/angelic/issue facts, then unresolved cases get co-change files, bidirectional structural dependencies and latest pre-fix commit, then remaining bugs receive documentation and pre-fix resolved-issue context.
author_relationship_evidence: Paper explicitly links replication package in §I; repository README identifies exact paper and says it contains code, data, prompts, patch outputs and analysis notebooks.
license: No project-level license in GitHub API or root tree. Paper CC BY 4.0 is for the paper and does not explicitly license the source repository.
exact_models: Llama 3.3 (70B per paper) and GPT-4o-mini; LangChain project-knowledge QA agent uses GPT-4o-mini.
n=10 outputs per prompt; Pass@1/3/5. No immutable model snapshot or full provider configuration pinned in README.
weights_status: No fine-tuning. Llama 3.3 weights may be run locally but require large 70B hardware; GPT-4o-mini and the project-level QA agent require hosted API. Cached generated patches/results are included.
evaluation_route: Public notebook package: main.ipynb extracts layered context, generate_prompts.ipynb builds prompts, run_patches.ipynb runs/organizes model patches, analysis.ipynb analyzes results. Repo contains per-bug data/prompts/patches, 314-row bug annotations and eight 314-row results CSVs. Category counts match paper Table I (187 anomaly, 47 network, 34 configuration, 28 GUI, 16 performance, 2 permission/deprecation). Static inspection only; no notebook execution or model call.
blockers: No project-level license declared for code/data despite paper CC BY 4.0; check reuse terms before adapting notebooks.

README dependencies are unpinned and there is no lockfile; notebooks use LangChain/HuggingFace/OpenAI calls and require environment reconstruction. Full regeneration needs GPT-4o-mini API and high-memory 70B Llama inference; the paper reports no total cost.
The paper reports full annotations/results and patch outputs, making result-level verification practical, but exact inference/provider snapshots and environment are not frozen.

Bug classes are adapted from Catolino et al. and represent broad software issue types; this is not a causal root-cause taxonomy. Manual labeling: first round Cohen κ=.45, after clarification κ=.8 on next 50; remaining 214 split between two annotators.
Use of function-granular perfect fault localization makes the reported repair rates optimistic relative to an end-to-end diagnosis setting.
concept_fit: High for bug-type/root-cause-analysis background and repository/project context layering, particularly BugsInPy; moderate for concept-guided test generation because it generates patches, not tests, and does not encode reusable behavioral concepts.
recommendation: Strongest directly relevant BugsInPy bug-type context artifact among reviewed papers: public replication package has annotations, prompts, patch outputs and analysis. Use as related-work/bug-type taxonomy source, not as a reproduction-test generator. Exact result analysis is feasible from included CSVs; full model rerun is conditional on license, API/70B compute, and rebuilding an unpinned notebook environment.
